correctness.rationale: Every rotation is distinct because c is unique. Counting ordered ab pairs in all suffixes yields the exact integer formula T=sum_r(r+t_r)(b-t_r). The monotone covariance inequality bounds this by the best constant integer t and its equality condition forces the stated block form. First-a contribution (t+1)(b-t)>=b gives the sharp least-positive gap and exhaustive equality cases. Direct literal verification checked 12,854 necklaces and 170,100 rotated words over all a,b in 1..7; this finite sample corroborates but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The first ternary circular Parikh family with one rare final-alphabet symbol has a nontrivial ordered-length-three count even at fixed Parikh content. Its exact maximum, complete optimizing necklaces, and sharp forbidden initial positive range are motivated invariant data for cyclic word inference and reveal a threshold in the optimizer run geometry. The fact is not just a finite computation or a binary composition identity.
